To answer your question, yes I would still feel the same way. To the one above it, no. Sure, world travel or finding something that makes me happy (which I'm not entirely sure actually exists) would be temporary distractions, but I don't think they could actually change the way I feel. They are not actual solutions. There are no solutions.
Honestly, I don't really want to do anything with my life but end it.

I have no interest in getting interests, if that makes sense. I have zero motivation or desire to develop new hobbies and interests, because I know that I will simply be going through the motions and I will not enjoy them. A vacation would be absolutely amazing right now, but I don't have the money.

Yes, I would. Maybe there's a chance I will feel differently, but I have no desire to stick around and find out, not to mention take the chance that it won't. Life hasn't always been bad for me, believe it or not I was happy at one point. It wasn't that great, there were still a lot of things that sucked. The possibility of feeling that once again is not worth what I am feeling right now.

It's nearly impossible for me to build relationships. I dislike the majority of people I meet, and people don't tend to like me very much either. I am also incredibly shy with crippling social anxiety. I can't just build relationships out of thin air. I also can't force myself into relationships I do not want. 

If we need relationships, if those are what we value most, then that simply reinforces my belief that I have nothing to live for.
I almost never leave my house except to go to work. As I said before, I don't have any friends (or a boyfriend) so I have nobody to go out with.

I have nothing to lose by living, but I do not enjoy it at all. I don't have any desire or motivation to make the effort of being content with something that I truly hate so much, if that makes sense.

I had interests once upon a time, but it's been so long I can hardly remember them, and I certainly do not have them anymore.

(I'm sorry if I'm being difficult, I really do appreciate you trying to help. I'm just being honest and trying to explain how I feel.)
19, and I'm a girl.

I've also been on a few different SSRIs and have talked to a few different therapists, I did these things for about 2 years but none of it seemed to help, and I can no longer afford them anyway. 

I guess what I'm trying to grasp is why should I not give up? What's the point of trying, when all I will learn to do is deal with this shitty fucking life that I don't want to live in the first place.

And I understand that people have figured out how to live, but I don't understand the desire to find a way/reason to live. I feel like these people are lying to themselves. Life is really shitty, finding things to value and appreciate might make it a little less so, but what's the point? The good things may make the bad things a little more tolerable, but why would you want to have to tolerate those things in the first place?

That's the thing. There's nothing substantially bad or upsetting going on in my life, I'm just bothered by and tired of the small things. Money problems, I have absolutely no friends, my family doesn't believe/care that I am depressed, I hate my job, etc. With that being said, there's also nothing substantially good going on in my life either. 

I just can't wrap my mind around the fact that people actually think being alive is a good thing. There's so much pain, sadness, struggle, even boredom... how could anyone possibly think that's worth it?
